scope: Riot's SEPTEMBER 14 mid-patch update of 18.2 and MetaTFT's lookup regenerated 2026-09-11, against the published 18.2 snapshot (lookup generated 2026-08-16). See 18.2b-review.md.

mappings.reason: The passive's tooltip reads this row as the chance to create a copy (<TFTCurveTable row="PercentChanceToPrint" format="percent"/>); it held exactly Riot's old 10/15/40%. Post-combat economy, read by no fight; mapped so the archive says what the game says. Star 4 (100%) is not in Riot's three-value line and stays. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-20) leblanc: 'Percent Chance To Print[ 10% / 15% / 30% ]'.

MagicDamageCalc1, the two small mushroom clusters, scales APDamage with Ability Power and held exactly Riot's old 60/90/135; the giant mushroom is BigMushroomDamage (135/200/310), untouched. Star 4 (230) is not in Riot's line and stays. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-20) teemo: 'AP Damage[ 55 / 82 / 130 ]'.

The flat term of GenericCalc1 (the armor ignored during Frenzy); it held Riot's old 15% at stars 1-2. One value for a 4-cost is its 1- and 2-star value; the 3-star formula is Riot's separate '3-star 4-costs' line and is not touched here. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-20) brambleback: 'During this time ignore 20% Armor'.

The Ability Power term of the same calculation (GenericCalc2); it held Riot's old 30% at stars 1-2. At the base 100 AP the total is unchanged (15 + 30 = 20 + 25 = 45%); with more AP it now grows more slowly. Stars 3-4 (70%/80%) are not in this line and stay.

The tooltip's 'leaves a trail for <RiftDuration> seconds'; it held Riot's old 4 s at stars 1-2 (20 s at 3 stars, which a single-value line for a 4-cost does not address). A duration the driver reads as a row, so the number changes and no timing code does. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-20) ashe: 'Rift Duration[ 3 / 3 / 20 ]'.

note.text: Draven Bounty Hunter:

dispositions.reason: Heading of the five Bounty Hunter quest lines, each of which has its own disposition.

note.text: Brambleback: Fixed a bug where his baseline Armor Ignore was higher than intended.

dispositions.reason: The engine never had a live bug: Frenzy ignores GenericCalc1 = FrenzyArmorIgnoreFlat + FrenzyArmorIgnorePercent x AP, read from the rows. The numbers Riot then states (20 + 25% AP) are mapped from the numeric line of the same update.

note.text: Brambleback: Fixed a bug where his Armor Ignore would decrease with increasing Ability Power.

dispositions.reason: The modeled armor ignore has always risen with Ability Power (the AP term is added, never subtracted), so there is nothing to undo. Frenzy's single refreshed buff remains the documented conservative policy.

note.text: Polymorph: All Polymorph Wisps can only be seen as the 1st Wisp of each Planning Phase.

dispositions.reason: Wisp offers are a planning-phase choice; no Wisp is part of a fight or a board here.

note.text: Fixed a bug where Auto Attack projectiles could get stuck on a dashing champion and deal much more damage than intended.

dispositions.reason: Attacks land after the windup as one instance of damage; there are no projectiles, dashes or collisions that could repeat one, so the fixed bug has no counterpart to remove.

note.text: Fixed a bug where Krug and Yorick would not spawn their summons when sacrificed by the Blackthorn Hex.

dispositions.reason: Blackthorn's sacrifice hex is left empty by every board (trait-models: the sacrifice is unmodeled), so neither unit is ever sacrificed and their on-death bodies are unaffected.

note.text: Fixed a bug where Thief’s Gloves would offer different items when re-equipped to another champion during the same round.

dispositions.reason: Thief's Gloves is outside the completed-item pool (random items); re-equipping between rounds is not simulated.

note.text: Fixed an issue where version mismatch would result in players being stuck on a spinner instead of being notified of a version mismatch with a popup modal

dispositions.reason: The one performance bullet that touches gameplay: effects restricted to a phase no longer linger past it. NOT modeled: trait-effects.json feeds DamageMult to every summoner and late.rs multiplies Azir's soldiers by it, so Azir's trait-context cells (low/high) overstate his Summoner bonus until the engine reads the new row. His bare cells, and therefore the default leaderboard, do not use the trait. Left to the engine's owners; recorded here so the gap is not silent.
